title: Apply for a licence to be reissued after being surrendered on medical grounds
summary: If you surrendered your licence on medical grounds and are now able to drive, you can apply for it to be reissued at a Service NSW Centre.
intro: If you had to surrender your licence on medical grounds and you're now able to drive again, you can visit a Service NSW Centre and apply for your licence to be reissued.
who_can_apply: You must have surrendered your licence on medical grounds.
You must now be able to drive again.
what_you_need: Your licence (if you have it) or proof of identity
A medical certificate signed by a medical practitioner, showing you meet the requirements to be reissued with your licence

how_to_steps.text: Make sure you have all your documentation.
Visit a service centre and submit your application.

more_info.text: Renewal notices are posted generally within 6 weeks of the card's expiry date.
For driver licence renewals or applications, a receipt is provided that allows you to drive until the card arrives in the post. The receipt is valid for 2 months.

faqs.q: What do I need to apply for a reissued licence?
faqs.a: You need your licence (if you have it) or proof of identity, a medical certificate signed by a medical practitioner, and the 'Licence Application' PDF form.

faqs.q: Where do I submit my application?
faqs.a: You must visit a Service NSW Centre to submit your application.

faqs.q: What is the first step in the application process?
faqs.a: First, select the 'Download PDF form' button and complete the form.
